name: Peace of God movement
summary: Beginning with the Council of Charroux (989), a series of synods in Aquitaine and Burgundy promulgate sacral protections for non-combatants, clergy, pilgrims, peasants, under threat of excommunication. The movement spreads across France and into Catalonia and northern Italy over the following half-century.

_quarry.structural_significance: First systematic European attempt to restrict legitimate violence by sacral sanction rather than secular force; later channelled into the Truce of God movement and, ultimately, the Crusading ideology of legitimate Christian violence outside Latin Christendom.
